questions.question: What is the actor model's fundamental rule about inter-actor communication?
options: Actors can share memory but must use locks
Actors communicate ONLY by sending messages; no shared memory is ever directly accessed
Actors can call each other's methods synchronously
Actors communicate via a shared database
questions.explanation: In the actor model, two actors can never share memory directly. All interaction is through message passing: each actor has a private inbox and receives messages from other actors who can only send, never read or write the actor's state directly.

questions.question: What are AutoGen v0.4's three API layers?
options: Input, Processing, Output
Core (low-level actor framework), AgentChat (task-driven high-level API), Extensions (integrations)
Client, Server, Database
Model, View, Controller
questions.explanation: AutoGen v0.4 has three layers: Core (AgentRuntime, Agent, Message, Topic — the low-level actor framework), AgentChat (AssistantAgent, UserProxyAgent, RoundRobinGroupChat, SelectorGroupChat — high-level task API), and Extensions (OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure, tools, memory integrations).

questions.question: Why does decoupling message delivery from handling provide fault isolation in AutoGen v0.4?
options: Messages are encrypted so failures cannot propagate
If Agent B crashes, the runtime catches the failure in B's handler without crashing Agent A, which sent the message
The runtime automatically retries failed messages
Agents run in separate processes by default
questions.explanation: When A calls send(agent_b, msg), it returns immediately. If B's handler raises, the runtime catches it in B's isolated context — Agent A has already moved on. B's crash is contained; A continues processing its own inbox.

questions.question: What is Magentic-One?
options: AutoGen's next-generation model
A reference multi-agent team for web browsing, code execution, and file handling built on AgentChat
AutoGen's visual debugging tool
A benchmarking suite for multi-agent systems
questions.explanation: Magentic-One is the reference multi-agent team in AutoGen v0.4, built on AgentChat, designed for web browsing, code execution, and file handling tasks.

questions.question: What is the current status of AutoGen v0.4 in early 2026?
options: Actively developed with new features being added weekly
In maintenance mode; Microsoft has shifted active development to the Microsoft Agent Framework
Deprecated and no longer supported
Being merged into LangChain
questions.explanation: Early 2026: AutoGen v0.7.x is stable for research and prototyping, but Microsoft has shifted active development to the Microsoft Agent Framework (public preview October 1, 2025; 1.0 GA targeted end of Q1 2026). AutoGen patterns port forward cleanly.

questions.question: What built-in observability does AutoGen v0.4 provide?
options: Custom proprietary tracing format only readable in Visual Studio
OpenTelemetry support with spans per message carrying gen_ai.* attributes per OTel GenAI semantic conventions
Logging to a plain text file
No built-in observability; you must add your own
questions.explanation: AutoGen v0.4 has built-in OpenTelemetry support. Every message emits a span; tool calls carry gen_ai.* attributes per the 2026 OTel GenAI semantic conventions (Lesson 23).
